newsitem.title: USA: Officers give account of New York plot tip.
newsitem.headline: Officers give account of New York plot tip.

text.p: The policemen who were tipped off last week about the alleged New York subway bomb plot said on Tuesday the man who walked up to them "seemed legitimate" and thus began a dramatic operation to arrest the suspects.

Officials who honoured the two officers at a news conference declined to comment on the man's identity or on reports that one of two men arrested had left a note calling for the release of Islamic or Arab militants from U.S. and Israeli jails.

The New York Post and ABC News have quoted investigators as saying that the note demanded the release of Ramzi Yousef, alleged mastermind of the 1993 World Trade Centre bombing and whose trial opened in Manhattan federal court on Tuesday.

Others mentioned included Sheikhh Omar Abdel Rahman, the Egyptian cleric jailed for life for plotting to bomb New York landmarks, bridges and tunnels, the Post reported. It said the name of Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, founder of the radical Palestinian group Hamas and best known for suicide bombing attacks in Israel, was also in the note.
"It was almost a state of shock for us, especially as things escalated as they did," said one of the officers, 34-year-old John Kowalchuk of the Long Island Rail Road Police.
He said he and his partner, police officer Eric Huber, were on routine patrol on Wednesday night when the man walked up to them and gave them the information.
The officers contacted the New York City police through their headquarters. They declined to comment on any details about the man or specific information he gave them.
"He just seemed legitimate to us, we both agreed that the guy seemed real, it didn't seem like he was making it up," Huber, 29, said in his account of the tip-off.

The two suspects, Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, 23, and Lafi Khalil, 22, were shot and wounded by police as they were arrested in a dawn raid on Thursday on a ramshackle Brooklyn apartment. Police seized five potentially-deadly pipe bombs.
Investigators believe the suspects were only hours away from bombing the Atlantic Avenue subway station in Brooklyn, which also serves the Long Island Rail Road.
Abu Mezer and Khalil have been charged with conspiracy and are under guard in a New York hospital. A third man was being held on an immigration charge, but authorities have not divulged his name.

Tuesday's news conference in the New York office of Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato was the first official acknowledgment of the tip that apparently foiled the bombing. Two officers who took part in the raid were honoured by New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Saturday.
"We weren't ready to reveal their part in terms of the investigation," Giuliani told reporters. "The FBI is still investigating."
